notes:
I don't have any commentary notes for you yet. My only attempt to fetch the sources failed, and I wasn't allowed to make any more web calls after that.

**What happened:** I tried to open six pages at once:
- Enduring Word on Jeremiah 51: https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/jeremiah-51/
- Bible Hub's commentary pages for verses 44, 45, 59, 63 and 64 (these collect Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and others), e.g. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/jeremiah/51-44.htm

The tool didn't send back the pages in a form I could read, and my web access then ran out for this turn. So I haven't read a single page.

**Why there are no notes:** You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, give a link for every point and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I read nothing, anything I wrote about verses 44–64 would come from memory with nothing to cite. That would break your rules, so I've left it all out.

**If you ask me again in a new message, I'll:**
1. Read the traditional verse-by-verse sources: Enduring Word, Bible Hub's pages for each verse from 44 to 64, StudyLight (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary) and Precept Austin.
2. Look for real differences between Protestant traditions. Likely places are v. 45 ("Come out of her, My people", often linked to Revelation 18:4) and vv. 62–64 (Babylon sinking "never to rise again", and whether that has already happened or is still to come).
3. Check NET Bible notes, Bible Odyssey, New Advent and the other alternative-view sites, but only include them where they actually discuss these verses.
4. Write the notes verse by verse, with a URL for each point.
